text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Swiss group Clariant will absorb the specialty chemicals business of Germany's Hoechst AG, becoming a world market leader in specialty chemicals. They expect their new company to achieve sales of eight billion Swiss francs in 1997.
- Shell International Ltd. plans to sell its Swiss refinery in Cressier as part of a European restructuring programme.
- Mikron technology group expects profits to rise to 14 million Swiss francs for the 1996/97 fiscal year ending January 31.
- The majority of state employees in Zurich will get three percent wage cuts and receive no raises for inflation in 1997.
- Rolf Zinkernagel, head of the Institute for Experimental Immunology at the University of Zurich, received the Nobel prize for medicine on Tuesday in Stockholm.
- Fashion and travel group Charles Voegele expects sales of one billion Swiss francs for the current year and plans to open between 30 and 40 new shops in 1997.
- The Swiss economy is expected to remain weak in 1997, according to the latest report by the Commission.
